verses.1: Look! On the mountains, there are feet that emit a joyful sound. It’s the sound of the Jewish people celebrating their holidays. May they be safe and protected from harm. For no one will ever again cause any trouble to you. All of this is a sign of protection.
verses.2: From your face rose a monster with terrifying features. It rushed forward with great force, possessing immense power.
verses.3: For Jehovah has restored Jacob’s glory, just as Israel’s glory was restored. For they are now whole again, and their songs have been silenced.
verses.4: Their guards were men from the army; they were killed by fire from the chariots on the day of their preparation and attack.
verses.5: At the edges, they cried out loudly; their voices echoed through the vast spaces around them. They were like lightning bolts that shone brightly in the darkness.
verses.6: Their great leaders will be defeated in their attempts. They will be quickly defeated, and their plans will fail.
verses.7: The gates of the rivers opened, and the palace was filled with light.
verses.8: And their voices rose high, and their songs echoed like the sound of summer winds upon their hearts.
verses.9: And there were visions of waters from its depths. And those miracles took place; they stood there, without any direction or guidance.
verses.10: It’s gold, it’s silver—but there’s no end to its beauty. It’s the most wonderful thing of all.
verses.11: Bukah, Mebukah, Mebulakah… The heart is filled with sorrow and pain. All my gifts are wasted in vain. Their faces are covered with shame.
verses.12: What a shame it is that Arion and his companions were lost. They went there, but no one came to save them.
verses.13: The lion hunts its prey with its claws, and it clamps down on its prey’s throat. Its fur and fangs are covered with poison.
verses.14: I am Yours, O LORD, with all Your armies. I will eat the thorns of your paths. I have known from the land of your captivity that no one will hear anymore the voice of those who mock.
